title: Redwood discovery - Ironclad Payments - latency & throughput
next_steps: Send Dedicated vs Hosted pricing + latency SLO matrix

transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-03-24 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~55m
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Mark Chen (CTO - Ironclad), Lena Rodrigues (Head of Platform), Omar Malik (SRE), Priya Singh (Product)

Summary (auto): quick discovery on latency/throughput needs for payments product; evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; focus on p95 targets, peak concurrency, streaming requirements, token/sec benchmarks. Action items and next steps captured at end.

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you taking the time. I'm Samira, AE at Redwood, this is Diego our solutions engineer. Quick intros?
[00:10] Mark: Hey, Mark Chen, CTO at Ironclad Payments. We've been doing payments orchestration for mid-market merchants. We're looking at adding LLM features for fraud signals and real-time chat ops.
[00:20] Lena: Lena, platform lead. Mainly focused on latency and safety constraints.
[00:25] Diego: Great, quick agenda — understand your SLAs, concurrency patterns, streaming needs, sizing (token/sec), and then map to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options.
[00:33] Omar: Quick note, we have strict PCI-adjacent controls, can't send card numbers to 3rd party without tokenization, so we care a lot about private or VPC options and KMS.
[00:45] Samira: Absolutely, we can cover Private deployment and our KMS integrations. Before that, what's your p95 target for real-time use cases?
[00:52] Priya: For the chat experience, p95 needs to be sub-300ms for short prompts — that's the target we promised product. For the fraud signal pipeline, p95 can be up to 1s but throughput is heavier, thousands of reqs per minute during peak.
[01:05] Diego: Got it. Sub-300ms p95 is aggressive but feasible depending on model size and hosting mode. Can you share typical prompt lengths / tokens?
[01:12] Mark: Chat prompts average ~60 tokens in, ~120 tokens out when streaming; fraud checks are short, 20 in, 40 out, but we run them at 1200 concurrent checks during batch peaks.
[01:25] Diego: So two workload profiles: low-latency streaming chat with streaming tokens and mid-size outputs, and a high-concurrency inference workload for fraud checks. Do you currently have any throughput benchmarks? token/sec numbers?
[01:37] Lena: We ran ad-hoc in-house tests on 4xA10g nodes, saw roughly 12k tokens/sec aggregated but p95 was spiky — sometimes 600ms for small chats under load. We haven't tuned KV cache or batching.
[01:50] Diego: Makes sense. Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput; Private gives full control in your VPC/on-prem with KMS. Hosted is easiest but for p95 300ms you might need dedicated capacity or a smaller model variant with quantization.
[02:05] Samira: A key lever is model selection and quantization — smaller, optimized open models or quantized variants drop latency a lot. Also continuous batching and prefix caching helps throughput.
[02:15] Mark: Can you explain prefix or KV cache a bit? Our folks used the term but not sure how it affects streaming latency.
[02:21] Diego: Sure — KV cache stores past key/value attention states so if users send follow-up prompts in a session, we don't recompute the prefix. For streaming, that reduces tokens-per-request compute and keeps p95 down. For brand-new prompts it's less effective, but for chat sessions it's great.
[02:40] Omar: We're worried about cold-starts and autoscaling causing tail latency. Our traffic is bursty with batch job windows. How does Redwood handle scaling and warm pools?
[02:49] Diego: Dedicated supports configurable warm pools and burst capacity. Auto-scaler can pre-warm machines based on traffic patterns. For Hosted, we have regional routing and fallbacks but less control over reserved warm capacity. Private gives you the most control but you manage the warm pool.
[03:05] Priya: And what about streaming token/sec metrics? We want to benchmark realistic streaming throughput, like x tokens/sec per GPU and aggregate.
[03:12] Diego: For a 30B quantized model on A100, you're often in the 20-50k tokens/sec per GPU range depending on batch sizes and sequence length; smaller models on T4/A10 can be 8-15k tokens/sec. But these are noisy numbers — we prefer to run a benchmark using your exact prompt shapes and concurrency.
[03:30] Samira: We'll propose a benchmark plan: you run a replay of 1 hour of production traces (or synthetic with similar token distributions), we run across Hosted (where possible) and Dedicated config, measure p50/p95/p99, token/sec, CPU/GPU utilization.
[03:43] Mark: Sounds good. On SLAs — if we commit to Dedicated, what's the latency SLO guarantee?
[03:48] Diego: We publish per-model performance profiles and Dedicated offers SLA-backed uptime and latency targets tied to configured instance types and warm pool settings. Exact p95 guarantees depend on the configuration; we'll share the SLO matrix.
[03:58] Lena: Security — we need SOC2/ISO, audit logs, SSO, and KMS with HSM support. Can Private cover air-gapped?
[04:06] Samira: Yes — Private is available as VPC or on-prem. We support KMS integrations and audit logs; air-gapped on-prem deployments are something we can discuss with our infra team for enterprise contracts. We'll share the security pack.
[04:20] Omar: Another concern: model fallbacks. If our heavy model is down, can requests route to a smaller model automatically? We don't want degraded UX spikes.
[04:26] Diego: Smart routing supports fallback to compatible model variants by policy — e.g., route to a 7B quantized variant with slightly lower quality but faster latency, and we can do A/B or canary rollouts.
[04:36] Mark: Okay, so for cost tradeoffs: how much cheaper is Dedicated per token compared to Hosted? Ballpark?
[04:42] Samira: Generally Dedicated reduces unit costs especially at scale due to reserved capacity and better batching; we'll send a pricing matrix tuned to your expected QPS and token mix. For the fraud checks (lots of short requests), optimizing batching and enabling KV/cache can drive big savings.
[04:58] Priya: For the benchmark plan, timeline? We need numbers by early April to decide on a pilot.
[05:03] Samira: We can kickoff the benchmark next week — Diego will send the plan and trace template today, you can share a sample trace and we'll schedule the runs. Results in about 5 business days per configuration.
[05:12] Diego: Quick note on telemetry — if you run the trace in your environment we can ingest traces (anonymized) and run the token/sec profile with our harness; please strip any PCI data.
[05:22] Mark: We'll tokenise PII and card data before sharing.
[05:25] Omar: One more technical — do you support structured streaming and partial tokens flush? We need streaming chunks to the client as tokens generate.
[05:33] Diego: Yes, Redwood supports streaming responses and partial token flushes, plus function/tool calling patterns for structured outputs. You can stream plus call hooks to commit results.
[05:42] Priya: Good. Also curious about concurrency limits per connection — we have 10k simultaneous websocket connections during peaks. Can Redwood handle that?
[05:49] Diego: Websockets are supported; concurrency at scale is solved via autoscaling and connection routing. For 10k concurrent streams, Dedicated with multiple GPU nodes and a proper load balancer is recommended. We'll map your concurrency to instance counts in the sizing doc.
[06:05] Samira: I'm going to capture some of the p95 targets you mentioned: chat sub-300ms (p95) on 120-token outputs, fraud checks p95 up to 1s but need high concurrency (1,200 concurrent), and bursts to 10k websocket connections. Anything else?
[06:18] Mark: Also regional residency — EU traffic must stay in EU. We need region routing and data residency controls.
[06:24] Samira: Noted. Redwood supports regional routing and Private in-region deployments for residency controls.
[06:30] Diego: A few more performance details — quantization can reduce memory footprint and improve throughput; however, some models see small quality regressions. We'll propose model candidates (7B/13B/30B quantized) and run evals on your prompts to check quality/latency tradeoffs.
[06:45] Lena: For the fraud checks we care about deterministic outputs for audit. Any caveats with quantization and determinism?
[06:52] Diego: Quantization doesn't inherently make outputs non-deterministic; sampling settings do. For deterministic runs, use greedy/beam decode and fixed seeds. We'll include that in the benchmark.
[07:02] Samira: Alright, let's walk through action items — Diego will own the benchmark plan, Samira will send pricing and security docs, Mark will provide traces and a list of top 100 prompt shapes.
[07:12] Mark: Yep, I'll get a sanitized trace and prompt samples by Friday.
[07:16] Priya: We'll want a follow-up where Se and infra are present to review the Dedicated sizing — week of 3/30 works.
[07:22] Diego: I'll schedule that. Also we'll propose two pilot configs: Hosted quick test (smaller model), and Dedicated pilot with 2-node warm pool.
[07:30] [Crosstalk] Lena: One more quick question — logging retention and access controls?
[07:35] Samira: We support configurable retention for logs in Redwood Console for Hosted and Dedicated; for Private you manage retention in your environment but we provide audit hooks.
[07:45] Diego: Also a note: when measuring p95 for streaming, we'll measure end-to-end time to first token and time to last token; sometimes teams focus only on end-of-stream which hides perceived latency.
[07:58] Mark: Good call. We'll want first-token latency to be prioritized.
[08:04] Samira: Cool. Quick recap of next steps and owners:
[08:08] - Diego: benchmark plan + trace template (send today)
[08:12] - Samira: Dedicated vs Hosted pricing + latency SLO matrix + SOC2 whitepaper (send EOD)
[08:16] - Mark/Omar: provide sanitized traces and top-100 prompt shapes (by Fri)
[08:20] - Schedule infra deep-dive (Samira/Diego to propose week of 3/30)

[08:25] Mark: That all sounds good. Any blockers?
[08:28] Samira: None on our side. We'll include a suggested Dedicated config for 10k websocket targets and 1.2k fraud concurrency.
[08:35] Diego: We'll also include recommended model variants and quantization profiles and note expected token/sec per GPU in the report.
[08:40] Lena: Thanks team.
[08:42] Samira: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and plan.

Action items (captured):
- "Diego Alvarez: Share benchmark plan and trace template (due: 2026-03-24 EOD)"
- "Samira Patel: Send Dedicated vs Hosted pricing + latency SLO matrix + security pack (due: 2026-03-25)"

Notes and misc:
- Discussion covered p95 targets (chat <300ms, fraud up to 1s), concurrency (1,200 concurrent fraud checks), streaming requirements (first-token latency prioritized), token/sec baselines (in-house 12k tokens/sec observed), recommended benchmarking across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Competitors mentioned: Anthropic and OpenAI for managed endpoints; customer also comparing to in-house GPU infra.
- Security: PCI adjacency concerns, KMS/HSM, SOC2/ISO required, data residency EU.

References shared during call: "benchmark-plan-template.xlsx" (link placeholder), "SOC2-whitepaper.pdf" (to be shared), "pricing-latency-matrix.csv" (to be shared).

End of transcript.
